hook: The premise fits in one sentence you will not forget: breakfast is an anomaly, and nobody has ever actually eaten it. The file then sends test subjects in on memory-boosting drugs to find out where people really go during that meal. Expect suffocation, stabbing and a bleak final log.
whyItMatters: SCP-4144 turns something universal and ordinary into an antimemetic cover story, which is why its containment is about neural networks and memory drugs rather than walls. The discovery through mismatched image-recognition tags is a neat touch: a machine catches what human perception has been edited to skip. Its structure moves from vague test reports to a clear camera record, so each section shows a little more than the last.
thingsToNotice:
Each early subject describes the same experience in fragments: a fall through darkness into a fluid-filled sac, a stab wound ringed by an antimemetic pattern, drowning, then waking with the intended meal already in their stomach. D-748 goes in with a suit and a knife, cuts his way out, and the footage shows rows of hundreds of sacs, screams followed by splashes, and a pit of brown fluid that analysis later breaks down into lactose, soy, wheat and rice products, animal proteins and fruit fibre.

The featureless foam figures drag D-748 to a white, silently beating heart, a new one steps out of it, has a face resembling his painted on, and drives a tube-linked spike into his abdomen. Back in the test chamber his stand-in suddenly attacks the guards with his cutlery and is shot, and the autopsy finds a body made entirely of extruded polystyrene foam wearing his real gear and carrying the real samples and recordings.
